packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-06 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (blind first reader)

Exposure statement: Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this fragment. Visible modern pencil labels on the piece: "Stams, STA, Frg. 34r" (image-004), "Stams, STA, Frg. 34v" (image-010), and an older-looking pencil shelfmark "IX a/N 29" (image-005; on face 2 written vertically, image-010, read by me as "IVa/N 29" or "IXa/N 29"). This is a blind reading.

Method note (beyond the plain rules): I made contrast-enhanced and enlarged crops of the supplied tiles with a local Python/PIL script (scratch files only), and tested one crop mirrored to check whether the large textura on face 2 is a mirror-image offset (result inconclusive, see below). I opened nothing except PROMPT.md and this packet's image files. Line numbers are counted from the first text line visible in each image (a cut line at the top edge counts as line 1); approximate pixel y given for anchoring.

==================================================================
1. LAYOUT SURVEY
==================================================================
Object: a small parchment piece c. 7 x 6.5 cm (scale bar), with a vertical fold/crease and a sharp dark vertical line (looks like a ruled line or the edge where two layers/strips meet) dividing it into a left panel (c. 3.5 cm) and right panel (c. 3 cm). Small worm/stitch holes along the fold; a damaged notch at the left edge (face 1) / right edge (face 2).

FACE 1 (image-001 overview; tiles 002-005; label "34r"):
- Script: small, rapid Gothic cursive (looped ascenders, long descenders with hooks, many suspensions). Grey-brown ink. Not the same script as the large textura on face 2.
- Left panel: at the extreme left edge only line endings of a column survive (tiles 002/004, x~60-300): short words ending lines. Then a blank strip (margin/gutter with the fold), then a narrow column of short lines (tile 002/004 x~690-1080) of c. 17-18 lines. Right of the dark vertical line: the right panel, a column of longer cursive lines (tiles 003/005) of c. 22-24 lines, continuing over the left panel's narrow column at the same line spacing (it is possible the narrow column and the right column are the same text block interrupted by the vertical line; uncertain).
- An enlarged "Per xp(istu)m" on a line of its own near the foot of the narrow column (image-004, y~720), larger letter forms than the surrounding text - observation: looks like a formula ending a prayer-like unit. "Qui iux(?)"/"Qui ...": an enlarged word at right in image-003 (y~575, "Qui(?) ...") apparently starting a new unit.
- No colour visible on face 1 except a tiny red dot (image-005 left, y~340). Fainter red specks on face 2 (below).

FACE 2 (image-006 overview; tiles 007-010; label "34v"):
- Two layers of writing are visible: (a) a smaller grey cursive (same type as face 1) running in horizontal lines across the left panel and a narrow column in the right panel, and (b) larger, browner Gothic textura letters (c. 2-3x the cursive x-height) under/among the cursive in the left panel and on the far right panel. The textura is fainter, blotchy and reads partly as mirror-like; I could not decide whether it is offset (transfer from a facing leaf), show-through from the other side, or an earlier erased text (palimpsest). Face 1 does not show this textura in the same position, so show-through of face 1 is unlikely. Mirrored crop did not read clearly either. Treat as unresolved.
- Red marks: small red strokes at the left margin of the left panel (image-007 y~615, y~900; image-009 y~120, y~205, y~430, y~580; one red stroke mid-line in image-009 y~370) and red touches in the textura line at the bottom (image-009 y~880). These look like red highlighting (rubricated capitals/paraphs) - which layer they belong to is uncertain; the bottom-of-page red is in the textura.
- Top line of left panel (image-007 y~70) has a larger-written word "Regula(?)" - possibly a heading; tentative.
- Right panel (image-008, image-010): narrow column of short cursive lines x~120-530, then a wide blank/stained area, then textura on the far right (image-008 x~730-1130, image-010 x~730-1150) with some cursive words interspersed (image-010 x~930-1140).

==================================================================
2. SELECTED SPANS AND UNREAD AREAS
==================================================================
Selected: face 1 narrow column (images 002, 004); face 1 right column lower part (image-005); face 1 right column top (image-003, partial); face 1 left-edge line endings (image-004). Face 2 left panel cursive lines (images 007, 009); face 2 right-panel narrow column (images 008, 010).
Unread: most of face 1 right column top half (image-003, heavy abrasion and a pale stain in the middle); the face 2 textura layer (not read beyond isolated letters); far-right face 2 cursive (image-010 x>930).
Suggest: UV/multispectral imaging for face 2 to separate the two layers; raking light on face 1 image-003.

4. LIMITATIONS
==================================================================
- The cursive is small, rapid and very abraded; most words could not be resolved and are given as "..." (seen but unread, not parchment loss). The few readings offered are individually uncertain and should not be used as search strings without re-reading.
- Face 2 has two superimposed layers (cursive and a larger textura); I did not separate them and did not read the textura.
- Column structure (whether the narrow column and right column on face 1 are one text block across the vertical line) is uncertain.
- Line numbering is approximate because of stains, overlaps between tiles (002/004, 003/005, 007/009, 008/010), and skewed lines.
